strings.name: Tsai Ing-wen
strings.summary: Tsai moved from legal teaching and trade negotiations into public affairs, leading the Mainland Affairs Council and serving as vice premier and DPP chair. Taiwan’s first woman president, she served from 2016 to 2024. Her administration pursued industrial, defence, pension and social-policy changes amid cross-strait tensions and policy disputes. After leaving office she continued international engagements on security and democratic cooperation.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Women’s political leadership
strings.highlights.h1.text: Became Taiwan’s first woman president and served two consecutive terms.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Industrial and social policy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Pursued industrial, defence and social-policy changes; same-sex marriage became legal in 2019 after legislative and judicial processes.

strings.timeline.t1.text: Addressed a US audience about mainland Chinese military pressure and Taiwan’s security as a former president.
